The CUDA implementation is a controlled port of the CPU solver, with separate
executables and pinned sources for each performance change. These checks verify
implementation/precision agreement; they do not establish spatial convergence,
physical boundary accuracy, or negligible magnetic divergence.

`validation/production_agreement_summary.json` records two complete25day real-map
coarse comparisons. Float64 CUDA and the controlled CPU reference have identical
final float32 snapshot arrays and12-digit probe n/v/flux values. Global LLF uses
5925steps/236 first-order fallbacks; split LLF uses6065steps/350 fallbacks. Minimum
timestep and all reported divergence statistics also match. Five tiny cases
exercise a uniform Cartesian state, radial wind, real time-varying maps, and both
flux variants with synthetic interval-electric-field input plus outer Br/Bt
scaling. Their snapshot fields and reported probes agree exactly at output
precision.

`validation/production_coarse_global_fp32_GTI_comparison.json` and the split
counterpart compare true float device evolution with verified float64 CUDA.
PN-only comet incident-flux mean/max-pointwise differences are−0.000353%/0.000762%
(global) and−0.0142%/0.0391% (split). Split takes one extra final step while retaining
350 fallback steps. Across every supplied probe, maximum flux differences are
0.00119% and0.316%, respectively. The full wide96 global precision check is
`validation/precision_wide96.json`, produced by the production runner: maximum PN
incident-flux difference0.00946%, density0.00993%, speed0.00179%; both precisions
use17293steps and972 fallbacks. This bounds roundoff at these tested grids; a
higher-grid precision effect has not been measured by this particular check.

`validation/cme_fp32_agreement.json` checks exact snapshot identity when the
optional cone table is absent and synthetic overlapping-cone agreement with the
controlled CPU reference. The synthetic field maxima differ by at most1.1e−5
relative. `validation/production_cme_coarse_fp32_GTI_comparison.json` adds a complete
25day nominal CME control:6076steps/344 fallbacks in both implementations, PN comet
incident-flux mean−0.00255%, maximum pointwise0.00431%. The cone is a conditional
n/v/T perturbation without flux-rope magnetic content; physical cone parameters
and density/duration assumptions remain separate uncertainties.

Every `validation/*_async_agreement.json` checks the execution-only flag-batching
optimization. Full coarse global, split and nominal CME cases have identical
snapshot arrays, probe file bytes, timestep, retry/fallback decisions and
divergence statistics versus the corresponding synchronous FP32 executable.
The37step wide96 short run is also identical. Failed intermediate states set a
persistent device flag; downstream kernels exit, and the host restores the
original conserved state before fallback/retry and before any probe is written.
No negative intermediate state is accepted or clipped.

The separate CUDA-event kernel benchmark writes JSON evidence without evolving
a production wind. At96×16×96, directional flux kernels take0.020–0.036ms in FP32
and0.226–0.243ms in FP64. At balanced192×64×192, tracked device data are898.45MB,
initial CFL timestep0.000500009day, and flux kernels0.327–0.343ms. The initial
state projects about50,000steps per25days; actual evolving states and fallback
counts determine final runtime. Wall times include driver launch/synchronization
and can be affected by other shared GPU processes; kernel speed ratios should
not be interpreted as complete-run speed ratios.

Reproduction is explicit: `make`, `make mhd_cuda_fp32`,
`make mhd_cuda_fp32_cme`, and `make mhd_cuda_fp32_async
mhd_cuda_fp32_async_cme`; then use the validation scripts described in README.md.
Regeneration scripts assert their source patches and save lineage hashes. They
never run implicitly through make or alter an earlier verified source/binary.
